summary: Anti-Nazi action series spanning Muse Software's stealth originals, id's FPS lineage, and MachineGames' modern alternate-history games.

entries.title: Castle Wolfenstein
entries.definitive_edition: MS-DOS port for preservation; Apple II for first-release study

emulation.notes: Apple II emulation is optional for original-release study.

primary.why: Apple II is the original release, but the MS-DOS port is the most practical current preservation route through DOSBox.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally preserved MS-DOS copy in DOSBox; use Apple II emulation for first-release historical study.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate this top-down stealth game with Wolfenstein 3D.

entries.title: Beyond Castle Wolfenstein

emulation.notes: Use original computer emulators for platform-history research.

primary.why: Beyond Castle Wolfenstein shipped on Apple II, Atari 8-bit, Commodore 64, and MS-DOS; DOSBox makes MS-DOS the practical archive route.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally preserved MS-DOS copy in DOSBox.

entries.remaster_caveats: Preserve separately from Castle Wolfenstein and the later FPS games.

entries.title: Wolfenstein 3D

primary.why: The PC release is the original and most complete route; console and mobile ports vary in levels, censorship, audio, or presentation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PC release through DOSBox or ECWolf/source-port setup with legally owned data files.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use source ports for comfort, but preserve original data and note gameplay-altering changes.

entries.title: Spear of Destiny
entries.definitive_edition: Spear of Destiny Super CD / current PC release

primary.version: Spear of Destiny Super CD / current PC release
primary.why: Spear of Destiny is the standalone Wolfenstein 3D companion; the PC Super CD/current package is the complete route with expansion content.
primary.how_to_play: Play through DOSBox or ECWolf/source-port setup with legally owned data.

entries.remaster_caveats: Catalog separately from Wolfenstein 3D because it is a standalone companion/prequel release.

entries.title: Return to Castle Wolfenstein
entries.definitive_edition: Windows main run plus console prequel mission

emulation.emulator: None for primary; PCSX2/xemu for secondary
emulation.notes: Play PC first; use console emulation/original hardware only for prequel content.

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the main campaign, while the PS2/Xbox console versions add a sourced prequel mission.
primary.how_to_play: Play Windows for the main run, then play one console version's Ras El-Hadid prequel mission as secondary content.

secondary.exclusive_content: Additional Ras El-Hadid / Egypt prequel mission in Operation Resurrection and Tides of War.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the console prequel mission only.
secondary.why: Both console versions include an additional single-player prequel mission absent from PC.

entries.remaster_caveats: Console versions are not the primary full playthrough, but their prequel content is worth secondary play.

primary.why: Enemy Territory is a free standalone multiplayer game on Windows, Linux, and Mac; Windows is the best current archive/capture route.
primary.how_to_play: Install the current community-supported Windows release and document server/mod state.

entries.title: Wolfenstein RPG

emulation.emulator: iOS device preservation / Java ME emulator for fallback
emulation.notes: Prefer preserved iOS install where possible.

primary.why: Wolfenstein RPG shipped first on Java ME/BREW, then iOS; the iOS version had improved sound and graphics and was more accessible.
primary.how_to_play: Preserve an existing iOS install/device if available; otherwise use Java ME/BREW preservation as historical backup.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile preservation title; verify device/OS availability.

entries.title: Wolfenstein

primary.why: Wolfenstein (2009) shipped on Windows, PS3, and Xbox 360; Windows is the highest-fidelity route, but the game is no longer available digitally.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned physical Windows copy and final patches; preserve installers/disc data because digital availability is limited.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster/current digital route is sourced.

primary.why: The New Order shipped across PC and two console generations; Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version through Steam, GOG, Epic, or Game Pass with the latest patch.

entries.title: Wolfenstein: The Old Blood

primary.why: The Old Blood shipped on Windows, PS4, and Xbox One; Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version through Steam, GOG, Epic, or Game Pass with the latest patch.

entries.remaster_caveats: Standalone prequel to The New Order; do not merge it into the main game entry.

entries.title: Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus

primary.why: The New Colossus shipped on Windows, PS4, Xbox One, and Switch; Windows with Freedom Chronicles DLC is the highest-fidelity complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Digital Deluxe/current release with Freedom Chronicles DLC installed and patch version noted.

entries.remaster_caveats: Switch is useful for portability but not the fidelity target.

entries.title: Wolfenstein: Cyberpilot

primary.why: Cyberpilot is a VR spin-off on Windows and PlayStation 4; Windows VR is the higher-fidelity headset route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows VR release with a compatible headset; treat it as a short side story, not a main campaign replacement.

entries.remaster_caveats: Short VR side story; catalog separately from Youngblood.

entries.title: Wolfenstein: Youngblood

primary.why: Youngblood shipped on Windows, PS4, Xbox One, Switch, and Stadia; Windows is the highest-fidelity route and supports co-op/Buddy Pass preservation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows version with a co-op partner where possible; document patch, edition, and Buddy Pass ownership.

entries.remaster_caveats: Document patch and co-op/Buddy Pass state.
